en: Alder Yard was behind construction fencing now.

New barriers divided the old industrial district into clean geometric parcels. A billboard showed a future riverside path where smiling young people in athletic clothes walked dogs across grass that did not yet exist.
Martin studied the billboard for a few seconds.
"Real estate sells the trees first. Plants them last."
They followed the old rail line along the east side of the fencing.
The brick walls were smoke-darkened to brown. The roof had been removed years ago, leaving only the steel skeleton. A municipal warning sign marked it as a hazardous structure.
Martin did not answer at once.
"Because you've made me look at something I haven't looked at in twenty-eight years. I'm trying to use fewer absolute words."
They circled to the north side.
Martin pointed to a sealed doorway.
"South parking area. First patrol officers found him there."
"He said Lena left him a message."
"I'm reminding you that missing evidence and an event not happening are not the same thing."
They reached a welded-shut side door.
He stepped back and looked at the wall.
"This door was supposed to be locked that night."
"Perimeter officers recorded every access point. North door breached. South door open. This east door had a crossbar set from inside."
"The body was found closest to this side."
"If the bar was set from inside, why didn't the person inside use this door?"
"Or maybe she didn't know the door was there."
Nora crouched near a blackened concrete drainage channel along the wall.
"So police had a gasoline purchase and an arson scene, but no container linking one to the other."
"They also had warehouse ash on Evan's shoes."
"And witnesses to an argument between them."
Martin looked at what remained of the warehouse.
"You know the version that reached court."
"Then give me the version before court."
For a long time he said nothing.
Wind moved through the exposed steel with a low hollow sound.
"The first twenty-four hours weren't that neat," he said. "Nobody knew why Evan was there. Nobody was certain who the body was. Nobody knew where Lena had gone that night."
"When everyone started believing the body was Lena."

"The body was badly burned. Routine DNA identification wasn't fast or standard the way people think of it now. The initial identification relied on estimated height and age, personal effects, work ID, and information from family."
Nora typed the answer into her phone.
"Don't write that as me admitting police identified the wrong body."
"I'm thinking a woman burned to death in a windowless warehouse twenty-eight years ago. Everyone gave her a name first, then started using that name to explain the rest of the evidence."
"Then give me one that's late enough."
At the parking lot, he stopped suddenly.
"Lena Zhou's forensic estimate was five foot six."
zh: Alder Yard已经被围了起来。新的施工围挡把旧工业区切成一块块几何形状。广告牌上画着未来的滨河步道，几个穿运动服的年轻人牵着狗，在一片根本还不存在的草坪上微笑。Martin站在广告牌前看了几秒。
他们从围挡东侧沿旧铁路走。
砖墙被烟熏成深褐色，屋顶早已拆掉，只剩钢梁骨架。门口挂着市政府危险建筑警告牌。
“因为你现在让我重新看一件我已经二十八年没重新看过的事。”
Martin指着一处已经封死的门洞。
“南面停车区。最早一批巡警到场时他在那里。”
“我只是在提醒你，证据不存在和事情没发生，不是一回事。”
他们走到一扇被焊死的侧门。
他向后退两步，看了看墙体。
“外围检查时，有警员记录所有出入口。北门破坏，南门打开，东侧这扇门从里面插着横栓。”
“尸体发现的位置离这里最近。”
“如果门从里面插着，里面的人为什么不从这里出去？”
诺拉蹲下，看见地面靠墙处仍残留一道烧黑的混凝土沟槽。
“所以警方有购买汽油的记录，有纵火现场，但没有连接两者的容器。”
“你知道的只是后来法庭上的版本。”
风从钢梁间穿过去，发出低低的呜声。
“案子刚开始的二十四小时里，没有人知道Evan为什么出现，没有人确定尸体是谁，也没人知道Lena当天晚上到底去了哪里。”
“当所有人开始相信尸体就是Lena以后。”
“烧毁严重。当年常规DNA鉴定没今天这么快。最初身份判断靠的是身高、年龄范围、随身物品、工作证和家属提供的信息。”
诺拉把这一句记进手机。
“别写得像我承认警方认错尸体。”
“我正在想的是，二十八年前一个没有窗的仓库里烧死了一个女人。所有人先给她一个名字，然后开始用那个名字解释其他证据。”
离开时，他走到停车场忽然停住。
“Lena Zhou的法医档案写的是五英尺六英寸。”
